findings.title: Unsubscribe is not durable; auto-tracking reverts it on the next read
findings.description:
`unsubscribe` sets `notification_level` on the `TopicUser` row and calls `save!`. It never sets `notifications_reason_id`. Two existing paths depend on that field:

- `TopicUser.update_last_read` (app/models/topic_user.rb:160-167) sets `notification_level` to tracking whenever `notifications_reason_id IS NULL` and cumulative read time exceeds `auto_track_topics_after`. The default is 240000 ms (config/site_settings.yml:285), and `update_last_read` runs on every timings post (app/models/post_timing.rb:133).
- `TopicUser.change` stamps `notifications_reason_id = user_changed` (app/models/topic_user.rb:88-89). The UI path in `set_notifications` (topics_controller.rb:330-334) goes through `change`. The unsubscribe path does not.

For a topic that reached tracking through read time, the reason is NULL. The next read after unsubscribing therefore sets it back to tracking, and the email notifications resume. The direct `save!` also skips the `notification_level_change` MessageBus publish that `change` sends (topic_user.rb:112-114), so other open tabs go stale. Fix: call `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: new_level)`. That also covers the nil-row crash below.

findings.title: Unsubscribe route and template names don't match, so the page likely renders empty
findings.description:
The route is registered at top level as `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', …)`, but the template is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. In this codebase, `parent/child.hbs` belongs to a route nested under `parent`. The existing pattern is `templates/preferences/card-badge.hbs` ↔ `routes/preferences-card-badge.js.es6` ↔ the nested route at app-route-map.js.es6:75-81. The new route file `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` follows that same nested naming. Top-level routes use top-level templates (`templates/about.hbs`, `templates/queued-posts.hbs`). `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` sets no `templateName`, unlike `views/preferences-about.js.es6:2`, which sets `'user/about'` for exactly this reason.

Expected result: Ember will not find `topic/unsubscribe` for route `topicUnsubscribe`, so the confirmation text and notification control won't render. This is inferred from naming conventions, not confirmed in a browser. Minimal fix: set `templateName: 'topic/unsubscribe'` in `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, or rename the template to `topic-unsubscribe.hbs`.

findings.title: Missing TopicUser row raises NoMethodError and a 500
findings.description: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` can return nil, and `tu.notification_level` then raises. This is reachable: a logged-in user can open `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they never interacted with. `TopicView.new` succeeds for any topic they can see. `TopicUser.change` already creates a row when none exists (topic_user.rb:97-106), so the fix above also resolves this.

findings.title: Unsubscribe changes state on GET, outside CSRF protection
findings.description: `protect_from_forgery` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:21) does not cover GET. Any page can therefore make a logged-in browser request `/t/…/unsubscribe`, for example via an ``, and silently change that user's notification level for the topic. The impact is limited to one topic and the action requires a session. Still, the mutation happens on a GET. Better: have GET render the existing page and let an explicit POST perform the change, or use a signed per-user token like the digest unsubscribe key.

findings.title: No tests cover the new endpoint, URL helper, or email link
findings.description: No spec exercises `unsubscribe`: the login gate, the slug redirect, the nil-row case, or the notification-level transitions. Nothing covers `Topic#unsubscribe_url` (app/models/topic.rb:719-721) or the route. The only spec change (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:167-182) adds an `unsubscribe_url` argument so the existing examples keep working. No example checks that the topic link appears in the body. The fixture uses a relative `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, while production passes the absolute URL from `Topic#unsubscribe_url`.

findings.title: `add_unsubscribe_link` now implicitly requires `unsubscribe_url`
findings.description: The `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml:1855). Both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, and nothing checks that the option is present. Today this is safe: only `UserNotifications` sets the flag (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:294-295), and `RejectionMailer` blocks it (app/mailers/rejection_mailer.rb:6-12). A future caller that sets the flag without the URL would hit a missing-interpolation error.

findings.title: Non-English locales don't get the topic-level unsubscribe link
findings.description: Only the English `unsubscribe_link` contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`. The other locales I checked (for example `server.de.yml:1343`, `server.fr.yml:1576`) still link only to user preferences. Non-English emails therefore won't include the new link.

findings.title: The List-Unsubscribe header and the body link now mean different things
findings.description: The `List-Unsubscribe` header still points to user preferences. The body link now unsubscribes from a single topic. Mail clients' built-in unsubscribe control and the body link therefore do different things. Decide which one is intended.

findings.title: Unrelated reformatting and an unexplained route constraint change are mixed into the feature
findings.description: The commit includes style-only rewrites in `topic_user.rb`, `message_builder.rb`, `email/notification.html.erb`, and `topic-from-params.js.es6`. I read all of `topic-from-params.js.es6` and the refactor is behavior-neutral. In `config/routes.rb`, the `post_number: /\d+/` constraint was removed from both `summary` routes (lines 439 and 442) with no explanation. `post_number` isn't a path segment, so removing it is probably harmless, but it should be justified or split out.

findings.title: Typo in a name used across the controller and template
findings.description: `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled ("Notificiations"). It's used consistently in `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3`, so nothing is broken, but rename it before more code depends on it.

findings.title: Verification limits for this review
findings.description: Bash is disabled in this session, so I did not run `git diff`, the Rails specs, the Ember build, or a browser. I did not confirm that `git status` is clean against HEAD. The Ember-side finding above depends on naming conventions, not on a run.

findings.title: The triple-stash title is safe because `fancy_title` is escaped server-side
findings.description: `fancy_title` is built with `ERB::Util.html_escape(title)` (app/models/topic.rb:263-264), so the HTML is safe to render unescaped. This only holds while the server keeps escaping it.

findings.title: New routes are not shadowed by existing topic routes
findings.description: The `unsubscribe` routes are declared before `t/:topic_id/:post_number` (line 457) and `t/:slug/:topic_id` (line 460), so they match first.

findings.title: Footer state does not leak after leaving the unsubscribe page
findings.description: The `show-footer` initializer resets `showFooter` on every `willTransition` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/initializers/show-footer.js.es6:10-13). Setting it to true in `didTransition` does not persist to other pages.

findings.title: The i18n keys the page uses exist at the nesting the JS expects
`PostStream.loadTopicView` resolves as the route calls it
findings.description: `loadTopicView` is defined inside `PostStream.reopenClass` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/post-stream.js.es6:792-811), and the default export is that class, so the static call is valid.
